analysis.investment_thesis: On the Magic Formula, this fails the critical "cheap" test — earnings yield is only ~2.3% (EBIT 35 Cr / EV ~1,534 Cr) at a P/E of 73, despite a decent but not exceptional ~20% return on capital. Growth is real but already more than priced in, and working-capital-driven negative FCF undermines the quality leg too.
key_strengths: Revenue and EBIT compounding at ~45% CAGR (FY22→FY25)
ROCE of ~23.65% is respectable for a small-cap industrial
Aerospace & defense tailwind with 68% promoter skin-in-the-game
key_risks: Earnings yield ~2.3% (EBIT 35 / EV ~1,534 Cr) — far below the 12%+ Magic Formula threshold
OCF negative 3 of last 4 years; cumulative FCF FY23-25 = -80 Cr vs 51 Cr profit
P/E 73 / P/B 10.9 leaves zero margin of safety if growth decelerates
red_flags: EBIT/EV ~2.3% — one of the worst earnings yields in the screen
Reported profits not converting to cash (OCF -3 Cr on 24 Cr PAT in FY25)
FY24 equity jumped 15→126 Cr (likely QIP/IPO dilution) boosting book but diluting per-share economics
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Magic Formula scoring: Earnings Yield = EBIT 35 / EV (1,515.8 mcap + 21 debt - 3 cash ≈ 1,534 Cr) = ~2.3%. That is bottom-decile cheapness — we want >12%. Return on Capital ≈ EBIT 35 / (Equity 148 + Debt 21 - Cash 3) ≈ 20.7%, which is good but not elite (>25% is what we want to pay up for). The formula demands BOTH legs; here only one is passable, so the ranking would be deep in the avoid bucket.

Beyond the formula, the cash-flow picture is a quality warning: OCF has been negative in three of the last four years (-9, -27, -3 Cr) while reported PAT grew from 8 to 24 Cr — classic working-capital bloat common in defense-component suppliers that get stretched by PSU receivables. The FY24 equity infusion (15→126 Cr) funded the growth, but at 10.9x book the market is already paying for several more years of 45% growth with no room for error. Pass.
